figures.alt: A Tlaxcalan drawing of a tall cross with two armed Spanish soldiers beside it and Tlaxcalan men in feathered headdresses gesturing toward it.
figures.caption: Lienzo de Tlaxcala, Cortes introducing Christianity; 1773 copy of a Tlaxcalan pictorial from the 1550s.

options.text: A scene from the Bible with no connection to the Americas.
options.misconception: The cross stands beside Spanish soldiers and Tlaxcalan men; the scene is the encounter in Mexico.

options.text: Tlaxcalan artists imposing Christianity on Spanish soldiers.
options.misconception: The soldiers stand armed beside the cross; the Tlaxcalans gesture toward it, they do not impose it.

options.text: A Spanish painter recording the conquest for the king of Spain.
options.misconception: The Lienzo was made by Tlaxcalan artists, not by a Spanish painter.

options.text: Tlaxcalans and Spaniards together at the cross, as Christianity arrives.

rationales.general:
1. Look at the center of the image. A tall cross stands there, marked INRI.
2. Look at who stands beside it. Armed Spanish soldiers on one side, Tlaxcalan men in feathered headdresses on the other.
3. Ask who drew it. Tlaxcalan artists, picturing the arrival of Christianity as they saw it.
4. Rule out the rest. No Spanish painter, no Bible scene alone, and no Tlaxcalan imposition fit the image.
Remember: to read an image, start with the center, then name who stands beside it.
rationales.D: The drawing centers on a tall cross with the instruments of the Passion, flanked by armed Spanish soldiers and Tlaxcalan men in feathered headdresses. Tlaxcalan artists pictured the arrival of Christianity as an event they witnessed.
rationales.A: The cross is not a Bible scene alone. Spanish soldiers and Tlaxcalan men stand beside it, which places it in Mexico at the encounter.
rationales.B: The armed soldiers show who held power. The Tlaxcalans gesture toward the cross; they do not impose it on anyone.
rationales.C: No Spanish painter made this. The Lienzo is a Tlaxcalan pictorial, drawn by Native artists in their own tradition.

stem: This drawing comes from the Lienzo de Tlaxcala, a pictorial made by Tlaxcalan artists in the 1550s. What does the image show?

stimulus.source_note: Lienzo de Tlaxcala, Hernan Cortes introducing Christianity; 1773 copy by Manuel de Yllanez of a Tlaxcalan pictorial from the 1550s; public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: This drawing is a 1773 copy of a Tlaxcalan pictorial from the 1550s, the Lienzo de Tlaxcala. At the center stands a tall cross marked INRI, with a ladder and the instruments of the Passion. Two armed Spanish soldiers stand beside the cross. On each side, Tlaxcalan men in feathered headdresses gesture toward the cross.
